expected.title: The Essence of Light: prakāśa vs vimarśa (V2-H)

review_note.ESSENCE_IS_TEXTUAL: G4-TC2 (vimarśa is the essence) is TEXTUALLY asserted by the C1 ('the claim is that the essence of light is the reflexive awareness... it is the manifestation's own nature'), NOT inferred from G4-DIST. So no exhaustiveness premise (a third feature accounting for non-inert manifestation) is smuggled in. If a reviewer disagrees that the C1 asserts the essence, G4-TC2 should be demoted to task_level B and its warrant re-examined.

expected.research_question: Is the essence of light bare showing (prakāśa) or reflexive awareness (vimarśa)?

nodes.text: Manifestation (prakāśa) is not a passive, inert light; it shows the world.
A light that merely showed the world without knowing that it showed it would be no different from crystal — it would reflect, but be inert.
nodes.boundary: the crystal is the inert contrast, not the subject of the doctrine

nodes.text: Bare showing (prakāśa alone) is distinct from self-aware manifesting; the distinguishing mark is self-awareness in the act (vimarśa).
The essence of light is the reflexive-awareness (vimarśa) — the light's own grasp of itself in the act of manifesting.
nodes.boundary: the reflexivity claim is established; the full powers/lordship account is developed in later vimarśas

nodes.text: What makes the light conscious (rather than a thing) is that it is aware of itself in the very act of manifesting.
Abhinavagupta identifies this self-knowing with the supreme speech (parā-vāk) and with the Lord's freedom (svātantrya) and lordship (aiśvarya).
nodes.boundary: REVIEW-2026-08-12-MODEL-1: this identification is a TEXTUAL/INTERPRETIVE GROUNDING (the C1 states it), NOT an inference derived from G4-CONC. No G4-INF-IC.

inferences.rationale: If manifestation were only bare showing (G4-TC1), it would be like crystal — it would reflect but not know it reflected (G4-CRYSTAL). Hence bare showing is distinct from self-aware manifesting (G4-DIST).
The distinguishing mark of consciousness is self-awareness in manifesting (G4-TC2 + G4-DIST); that is what makes the light conscious rather than a thing (G4-CONC).

boundary.text: The passage establishes that the essence of light is reflexive-awareness (vimarśa), not the bare showing of objects. It does NOT by itself establish the full account of the powers and the Lordship (developed in the following vimarśas, V2-I / V2-S), nor that language produces the self-grasp.
not_claiming: the full account of the powers and the Lordship
that language produces the self (language is its form, not its producer)

debate_frame.question: Is the essence of light bare showing (prakāśa) or reflexive awareness (vimarśa)?
debate_frame.object_of_dispute: the nature of light: bare manifestation (prakāśa) vs reflexive awareness (vimarśa)
shared_ground: a merely-inert showing would be unconscious
disputed_ground: whether the essence of light is the bare showing or the self-awareness

semantic_alignments.rationale: prakāśa = the light's showing of objects
vimarśa = the light's self-awareness in manifesting (the heart of the doctrine)
the whole distinction: showing ≠ self-aware showing; vimarśa is the essence, not an added quality
